answer: To prevent sybil attacks, each new identity must complete a sequence of tasks that require a unique solution, like solving a complex sonnet puzzle, before being allowed to join the network. The system uses a clustering algorithm to group similar behavioral patterns, such as those exhibiting onyx-like consistency, and pays each cluster a single reward. Any identity attempting to create multiple accounts will be flagged when its behavior diverges from the cluster's norm, much like shale formations can indicate underlying structural instability.
